raw.raw:
The Crossroads of Ashenveil smells of charred bone and cold iron, the ash-wind coming off the Blighted Reach carrying both in equal measure. Four roads meet here in the dying light, and three of them lead nowhere a sane man follows after dark — but Harn Blacktide has walked all four, has walked them in sleet and in summer heat and once in a blindfold on a bet, and he knows every rut and stone the way a man knows the lines of his own palm. The waystation at the crossroads corner is dark. No lantern, no smoke, no sound of the drover's mule that is always, always tethered outside — and the hire-board beside the door swings on a single nail, one manifest pinned there and flapping like a dying bird, stamped with a merchant's seal Harn does not recognize. Beneath the seal, in letters cut deep and deliberate as a brand, someone has written a single line: *GUIDE REQUIRED. URGENT. ASHENVEIL SOUTH. CARGO ALREADY MOVING.*

[LOCATION:The Crossroads of Ashenveil, The Blighted Reach]
[LOCATION_DESC:A desolate junction where four roads converge in the Blighted Reach. Ash-wind scours the bare earth. A waystation building squats at the corner, built from grey stone and old timber. A hire-board hangs beside the door. The horizon in every direction is scorched flat, with distant shapes that might be ruins or might be shadows.]
[LOCATION_SIZE:small|10]
[TIME:dusk]
[WEATHER:cold wind carrying ash]

Harn's longsword clears its scabbard with a sound like tearing cloth, the familiar weight settling into his fist. He shoulders the waystation door open and lets the ash-wind push in ahead of him, the better to see what flinches.

The interior is one long room, low-ceilinged, smelling of tallow and something beneath it, something sweet and wrong, like meat left in standing water. The station keeper's stool lies on its side. Two tin cups sit on the plank table, one still upright, one shattered, and the drink that spilled from it has dried dark and thick into the grain of the wood. Not wine. The wall behind the counter holds the usual freight records, nailed in rows, but every manifest dated within the last three weeks has been torn away, leaving only ragged paper tongues and bent nails.

[DICE:Perception check|17|success]

Behind the counter, wedged under the lowest shelf as though thrown there, or dragged, a body. Male, heavyset, dressed in the grey coat of a waystation keeper. His hands are bound behind him with leather cord and his face is pressed into the floor, but what stops Harn cold is the mark burned into the back of his neck. A circle. Inside it, a set of scales, perfectly rendered, the kind a counting-house uses. The brands edges are clean and deliberate. This was not done in haste.

[NPC:Waystation Keeper|dead, bound|victim]
[NPC_PRONOUN:Waystation Keeper|he/him]
[LORE:The Pale Ledger uses a burned scales-and-circle brand as a mark; the waystation keeper was murdered and all recent manifests torn away]
[QUEST:The Last Manifest|active|Trace the missing caravan's route south from the Crossroads of Ashenveil, reading the road for what went wrong]
[STORY_BEAT:Harn discovers the murdered waystation keeper and the Pale Ledger's brand, signalling the road has already turned hostile]

Harn takes the manifest from the hire-board in one pull, the nail shrieking as it gives. He carries it inside where the last grey light through the doorway is better than nothing, and he holds it flat against the plank table, away from the dark stain.

The document is good vellum, not the cheap pressed paper a waystation usually stocks. The handwriting is clerk-precise, every letter the same height, the kind of script that comes from years copying ledgers in a counting house. The cargo is listed as dry goods, salt brick, tallow, the dull bones of any legitimate freight run south through the Reach. But the weights are wrong. Harn has moved enough salt to know its tonnage by feel, and what is listed here would require oxen, not the two-horse team specified. Something heavier than salt filled those wagons.

[DICE:Investigation check|14|success]

The seal at the bottom is pressed deep into the vellum, a circle of pale wax the colour of old teeth. Inside it, the same scales-and-circle he found burned into the keeper's neck, rendered now in miniature. Beside the seal, a phrase in small capitals: *PALE LEDGER TRANSIT AUTHORITY.* Below that, a departure date three weeks past, and a single destination: *WAYMARK SEVEN, ASHENVEIL SOUTH ROAD.*

No guide's signature. The cargo was already moving before anyone was hired. Someone expected Harn specifically to find this.

[LORE:The missing caravan manifest lists false cargo weights, suggesting something heavier than salt; destination is Waymark Seven on the Ashenveil South Road; the Pale Ledger is named as a transit authority]
[QUEST_STEP:The Last Manifest|Examine the manifest at the waystation|true]

Harn sheathes the sword, crouches beside the keeper, and rolls him over with the flat efficiency of a man who has handled the dead before and holds no sentiment about it.

The keeper's face is older than Harn expected, deep-lined, a working man's face, and whatever killed him left no mark on the front of him. The binding cord is professional work, not a bandit's hasty knot but a sailor's hitch, the kind that tightens under struggle. Harn goes through the coat pockets with two fingers, methodical.

[DICE:Investigation check|12|success]

A folded paper, tucked inside the breast pocket, still warm from the body's last heat. Harn opens it. A personal letter, short, written in a different hand than the manifest, hurried and cramped where the vellum was careful. It reads: *They came before the Blacktide man arrived. Told me to leave the notice and say nothing. I will not. The wagons that passed through three weeks ago carried no salt. I heard sounds from inside the canvas. Not livestock. The Ledger's outrider said Waymark Seven is sealed now, that nobody walks south of it anymore. I am sending this to* and there it stops, torn across, the rest gone with whoever came back to silence him.

At the keeper's belt, a brass token. A route marker, the kind waystations stamp for verified guides. This one reads *ASHENVEIL SOUTH, SENIOR PASSAGE* and bears twenty years of thumb-polish on its face.

[ITEM_GAINED:Brass Route Marker]
[LORE:The sounds from inside the caravan wagons suggested living cargo, not goods; Waymark Seven on the Ashenveil South Road is reportedly sealed by the Pale Ledger]
[QUEST_STEP:The Last Manifest|Examine the manifest at the waystation|true]

The keeper stares back at Harn with the absolute patience of the dead, face slack, eyes fixed on the low ceiling, beyond all advice and companionship.

The ash-wind moves through the open door and shifts the torn paper tongues on the wall, and for a moment the only sound in the Blighted Reach is that dry, papery flutter. Harn has talked to corpses before, on bad roads and worse nights, but the road has never yet talked back.

He is alone at the Crossroads. That is the plain fact of it.

Outside, the last red smear of dusk is bleeding out of the western sky, and the Ashenveil South Road stretches away into dark country, straight as a scar across the flats. Three weeks of wheel-ruts pressed into that blighted earth, hardened now to iron in the cold. A caravan that should have had a guide never got one, carried something that breathed, and rolled south toward a waymark nobody walks past anymore.

The brass token in Harn's fist is warm from a dead man's belt. Twenty years of that same road under his boots, and somewhere out there in the dark it has turned into something he does not yet recognise.

He ought to start walking before the light is entirely gone.

The nod is all the keeper gets, and it is more than most. Harn steps over him, tucks the manifest inside his coat, and walks out into the last of the dying light.

[SUBLOCATION_LEAVE]

The east road is packed ash and old gravel, hard underfoot, the cold biting at the gap between his collar and his jaw. Grey Ford is three hours at a road-walker's pace, longer if the ash-wind picks up, and it is already picking up.
